author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boston College marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks with its annual Red Bandanna Game, honoring alumnus Welles Crowther during Friday night’s 28-21 football victory over Rutgers. The matchup carried a connection for both universities: Crowther graduated from Boston College, while Rutgers commemorated 37 alumni killed in the attacks.

Crowther, a former Boston College lacrosse player and volunteer firefighter, helped people escape the World Trade Center’s South Tower before he died. Survivors remembered the red bandanna covering his face as he guided them through smoke and returned to help others, giving the cloth lasting significance in the school’s memorial tradition.

Boston College players wore red-and-white paisley elements and “For Welles” on their uniforms. Rutgers incorporated the number 37 and American flag details into its tribute. Fans at Alumni Stadium also carried red bandannas and participated in a coordinated whiteout. The 2026 game was held on September 11 itself, giving the established campus tradition added meaning while linking the schools’ remembrance to service, courage and the alumni communities affected by the attacks.
dek: Boston College and Rutgers used uniforms and stadium tributes to remember Welles Crowther and alumni killed in the September 11 attacks.
headline: Boston College honors Welles Crowther in Red Bandanna Game
